episode.title: Resume partially delivered streams after retryable socket closure without duplicating output
episode.before: At parent commit 3d1eba935f6a75d9e67adf667002700c5c592ec2, the stream loop could replay a request only when the current attempt had produced no non-thought content. If a retryable socket-level transport error occurred after visible answer text had reached the caller, replay was rejected to avoid duplication and the transport error propagated. Text-only partial output was not durable history, so there was no continuation path that both preserved the caller's visible prefix and reconstructed the complete model turn.
episode.after: At d7c0d4ca7706ede8d1c8877a20343aa3e1d40bf5, retryable transport cuts with accumulated nonblank text and no function call enter a separately budgeted continuation path. Each continuation request temporarily appends the delivered model prefix and a fenced resume instruction, emits a continuation RETRY so consumers retain displayed text, deduplicates overlap at attempt boundaries, and merges the delivered prefix into the successful trailing model turn. Fresh-restart retries and reactive compression clear staged continuation state; function-call cuts and exhausted continuation budgets still propagate.
episode.diff: The change adds a three-attempt continuation budget and shared recovery-message construction; tracks per-attempt and accumulated delivered text plus function-call presence; distinguishes clean replay from continuation using accumulated visible output; creates request-only synthetic continuation turns; emits continuation-aware retry events; resets staged state whenever another recovery branch restarts from rebuilt/original contents; folds repeated overlap between attempts; and prepends the recovered prefix into durable history. The test suite adds scenarios for successful continuation, history reconstruction, repeated cuts, overlap removal, thought-only or empty later attempts, budget exhaustion, function-call exclusion, clean replay cases, and continuation supersession by other retry paths.

evidence_units.claim: Commit d7c0d4ca resolves issue #7832 through PR #7896 and states that long streams cut after visible output previously failed because replay was unsafe and unavailable.
evidence_units.source: issue-bundle.json linked_pull_requests[0] and commit_show_stat; commit d7c0d4ca7706ede8d1c8877a20343aa3e1d40bf5

evidence_units.claim: The parent implementation replayed curated transport failures only while the current attempt had yielded no non-thought content; otherwise it logged skipped_after_content and propagated the error.
evidence_units.source: git show 3d1eba935f6a75d9e67adf667002700c5c592ec2:packages/core/src/core/geminiChat.ts, stream transport retry branch around parent lines 2681-2720

evidence_units.claim: The change introduces maxContinuationRetries=3, separate accumulated/per-attempt continuation text, a continuation prefix, and attempt-boundary overlap folding.
evidence_units.source: git diff 3d1eba935f6a75d9e67adf667002700c5c592ec2 d7c0d4ca7706ede8d1c8877a20343aa3e1d40bf5 -- packages/core/src/core/geminiChat.ts; resulting lines 489-502 and 2527-2660

evidence_units.claim: A continuation attempt is admitted only for a retryable transport error with no yielded function call, nonblank accumulated text, and remaining continuation budget; it emits RETRY with isContinuation=true.
Continuation requests append the accumulated prefix as a synthetic model turn and a fenced resume instruction as a synthetic user turn without writing those turns to durable history.
On each failed attempt, delivered text is folded into the accumulated buffer through the existing recovery suffix helper, removing replayed overlap at the attempt boundary.
After a successful continuation, the delivered prefix is merged into the trailing model turn, preserving leading thought parts and deduplicating overlap with continuation text.
Fresh-restart recovery paths clear all continuation state, including ordinary replay and reactive compression, so request state and the caller's buffer-discarding retry event remain consistent.

The stream producer uses the pre-existing continuation-aware retry event shape, emitting isContinuation=true when the consumer must preserve already displayed text and plain RETRY when a fresh restart discards it.
evidence_units.source: git show d7c0d4ca7706ede8d1c8877a20343aa3e1d40bf5:packages/core/src/core/geminiChat.ts lines 2935-2943; same file also contains existing MAX_TOKENS continuation emissions around lines 3368 and 3448

evidence_units.claim: Tests verify that a visible prefix survives a socket cut, the next request carries the prefix and resume instruction, the retry is marked as a continuation, and caller output is delivered once in order.
Tests verify durable history reconstruction, absence of synthetic recovery instructions from history, overlap removal, repeated-cut accumulation, and correct placement around thought parts.
Tests verify bounded failure and exclusions: the fourth cut propagates after three continuations, and a cut containing a function call is not continued.

Tests verify recovery-path reconciliation: thought-only and blank initial output use clean replay; accumulated text remains in continuation mode when a later attempt yields only thought or nothing; fresh-restart invalid-stream recovery and reactive compression discard stale continuation state.
The commit record reports 277 geminiChat tests passing and TypeScript and ESLint checks clean after the final behavioral revisions.

candidate_atomics.name: route transport failure by delivered semantic output
candidate_atomics.description: Choose replay, continuation, or propagation using accumulated visible text, per-attempt output type, function-call presence, and bounded retry state rather than treating every emitted chunk equivalently.

semantic_action.intent: Recover retryable stream cuts without duplicating visible output or creating invalid tool-call sequencing.
semantic_action.pre_state: A streaming attempt ended with a classified retryable transport error, with observed output and retry counters available.
semantic_action.post_state: No visible accumulated text selects bounded clean replay; accumulated nonblank text without a function call selects bounded continuation; unsafe or exhausted cases propagate.
semantic_action.validation: Branch tests distinguish visible text, thought-only output, blank text, later empty/thinking attempts, function calls, and exhausted budgets.

candidate_atomics.name: stage an isolated continuation request
candidate_atomics.description: Construct the next request from the original contents plus request-only synthetic turns containing the delivered prefix and a resume instruction, while signaling consumers to retain displayed output.

semantic_action.intent: Ask the model to continue after already delivered output without replaying the original answer or polluting the transcript.
semantic_action.pre_state: Continuation routing has selected recovery and a nonblank delivered prefix is available.
semantic_action.post_state: The next attempt sees the delivered prefix and a fenced resume instruction; durable history remains unchanged by the synthetic turns; consumers receive a continuation-aware retry signal.
semantic_action.validation: The continuation test inspects the second request, retry event, ordered caller output, and durable history for absence of the injected instruction.

candidate_atomics.name: fold attempt output without replayed overlap
candidate_atomics.description: Accumulate output only at attempt boundaries and remove any suffix/prefix overlap replayed by an intermediate continuation attempt.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent repeated model tails from being embedded in later requests and durable history across multiple stream cuts.
semantic_action.pre_state: A continuation attempt has ended after delivering zero or more text chunks, possibly repeating the prior attempt's tail.
semantic_action.post_state: The accumulated continuation buffer contains every delivered fragment in order with cross-attempt overlap represented once.
semantic_action.validation: Tests cover final-attempt overlap, overlap from an intermediate cut attempt, and accumulation across repeated cuts.

candidate_atomics.name: restore complete durable response history
candidate_atomics.description: Merge the caller-visible prefix into the successful continuation turn, deduplicating overlap and retaining the model turn's thought/text part ordering.

semantic_action.intent: Keep durable conversation state consistent with the complete response already observed by the caller.
semantic_action.pre_state: A continuation attempt completed successfully, but durable history contains only that attempt's resumed portion while the earlier visible prefix is held separately.
semantic_action.post_state: The trailing model turn contains the complete response exactly once, synthetic continuation turns are absent, and thought parts retain their relative placement.
semantic_action.validation: History tests assert complete stitched text, overlap removal, no synthetic instruction leakage, merging after a leading thought, and insertion when no continuation text part exists.

candidate_atomics.name: clear continuation state when recovery strategy is superseded
candidate_atomics.description: Discard staged prefix and counters before any non-continuation restart that rebuilds or replays the request and tells consumers to drop existing output.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent caller-visible state and durable/request state from diverging when another recovery mechanism replaces an in-flight continuation.
semantic_action.pre_state: A continuation is staged, but a fresh-restart retry or reactive compression takes ownership and emits a non-continuation retry event.
semantic_action.post_state: The subsequent request contains no stale delivered prefix or continuation instruction, and successful history matches the clean restarted answer.
semantic_action.validation: Tests exercise invalid-stream fresh restart and reactive compression superseding a pending continuation, asserting the discarded prefix is absent from the next request and final history.

candidate_workflows.description: A partial-order recovery workflow for long-running streams: classify output semantics, continue from visible text when safe, deduplicate across repeated attempts, reconcile successful output into history, and reset staged state if another restart mechanism supersedes continuation.

unresolved_or_deferred: Continuation is intentionally not applicable after a yielded function call because inserting a user recovery turn would break the required function-call/function-response adjacency.
Recovery is bounded: after three continuation attempts the transport error propagates.
The implementation uses model-generated continuation rather than byte-exact transport resumption, so semantic continuation quality remains model-dependent.
A cross-project resolution pattern is deferred because this single episode cannot satisfy the required multi-repository support and holdout gates.

unresolved_questions: The GitHub bundle lacks the original issue body, comments, PR body, reviews, and status-check records; issue motivation and review rationale are therefore limited to the pinned commit message and checkout evidence.
The reported 277-test, TypeScript, and ESLint validation result comes from the commit record; this extraction did not independently execute the repository test suite.

No consumer-side file for isContinuation was available in the sparse checkout; call-site semantics are supported by the producer's pre-existing continuation event usage, implementation comments, and tests that assert plain versus continuation retries.
